paper.title: Asking Before Acting: Gather Information in Embodied Decision Making with Language Models
paper.central_claim: Asking Before Acting (ABA) lets an LLM agent proactively query external information sources in natural language while acting, improving performance and efficiency over baseline LLM agents; ABA-FT further improves hard tasks.

scope.note: LLM agent with an ask action in ALFWorld (text embodied), a Ravens UR5e arm (oracle captions) and a human-executed real-world demo. Kept in scope because a robot-arm manipulation loop is evaluated closed-loop; the harness is thin and the informant is privileged, flagged for aggregation.

evidence.quote: we propose \textit{Asking Before Acting} (ABA), a method that empowers the agent to proactively inquire with external sources for pertinent information using natural language during their interactions within the environment
evidence.support_explanation: Central operation: an ask action to external information sources.

evidence.quote: we show that LLM agents encounter challenges in efficiently gathering essential information, leading to suboptimal performance
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: information gathering in unfamiliar environments.

evidence.quote: are augmented with answers and questions respectively
evidence.support_explanation: Formal operation: state/action spaces are augmented with answers/questions.

evidence.quote: We term the identification procedure, i.e., why we posing such questions, as the metadata of the questions
evidence.support_explanation: ICL examples prepend manually labelled 'metadata' (rationale for asking) to each question.

evidence.quote: via another language model which is instructed to respond to questions based on the provided information
evidence.support_explanation: The information source is an LLM 'human model' H, not a human.

evidence.quote: we extract the information about the object placement from the simulator and transform it into a descriptive paragraph
evidence.support_explanation: H is fed simulator ground truth (privileged object placement) to answer; ReAct has no such channel.

evidence.quote: We test across 8 randomly sampled scenarios in ALFWorld with 5 questions each
evidence.support_explanation: Human-model accuracy check: 40 questions only.
H answers wrongly about 27.5% of the time (Vicuna-7B).

evidence.quote: The mean performance of ABA with GPT-3.5 is higher than the max performance of BUTLER in 12 out of 14 scenarios
evidence.support_explanation: Headline ALFWorld comparison with the IL baseline (BUTLER best-of-8 vs ABA mean).

evidence.quote: ABA also outperforms ReAct in all scenarios
evidence.support_explanation: Same backbone, same K=2 examples, same action scoring: ReAct vs ABA.

evidence.quote: ReAct / V7B mean of 5 ID 9\pm 7 8\pm 4 9\pm 3 4\pm 5 9\pm 8 4\pm 4 7\pm 3
evidence.support_explanation: ReAct with Vicuna-7B reaches 7% overall (ID), showing a very weak baseline.
ABA with GPT-3.5: 84 ID / 85 OOD overall, mean +- std over 3 seeds.

evidence.quote: ABA achieves more than 40 % performance gain compared to ReAct
evidence.support_explanation: Gain is larger for the smaller backbone (Vicuna-7B) than for GPT-3.5 (~20%).

evidence.quote: Length [Succ] 18.2\pm 9.7 11.5\pm 3.3 Length [All] 29.3\pm 17.1 16.9\pm 13.8 # Actions 13.1\pm 8.3 6.3\pm 2.6
evidence.support_explanation: Efficiency: fewer steps and physical actions despite the extra ask action.

evidence.quote: For a fair comparison, we use the same scoring method to select actions for both our method and ReAct
evidence.support_explanation: Action-scoring is matched between ABA and ReAct.

evidence.quote: For Ambiguous ALFWorld, we adjust the task descriptions and reward functions to introduce ambiguity
evidence.support_explanation: Authors built the ambiguous variant so that only asking resolves the task (by construction).

evidence.quote: But in this modified setting, the task is only deemed completed when a specific mug is put on the shelf
evidence.support_explanation: Success requires the specific object known only via the answer: ReAct cannot obtain this by design.

evidence.quote: we find that both ABA and ABA-FT consistently exhibit superior performance, while ReAct fails to complete the task in most scenarios
evidence.support_explanation: Ambiguous/Multiround results are shown only in Fig 2 (image); text sentence is the only readable evidence.

evidence.quote: we design a rule-based policy according to the PDDL planning trajectories provided along with the environment
evidence.support_explanation: ABA-FT data comes from a privileged rule-based expert using PDDL and ground-truth state, with templated questions.

evidence.quote: randomly inserting noisy actions at probability p=0.2
evidence.support_explanation: Noise injected into expert data; corrupted actions masked from the loss.

evidence.quote: we use LoRA ( Hu et al., 2021 ) with r=16 and a learning rate of 1e-5
evidence.support_explanation: ABA-FT training recipe (3000 / 6000 steps) is reported.

evidence.quote: we only use 1500 and 500 trajectories to finetune one model for all the tasks for each environment
evidence.support_explanation: ABA-FT data scale: 1500 / 500 trajectories.

evidence.quote: average success rate across 20 trails for each setting
evidence.support_explanation: Robot-arm tasks: 20 trials per setting, GPT-4 backbone, no CI.
Robot-arm results per configuration (x=3,4,5; y=2,3,4; x=4,y=3).

evidence.quote: Currently the module can access the simulator information and label the object type and its ground truth coordinates
evidence.support_explanation: Robot-arm observation captioner is oracle (privileged perception) for both arms of the comparison.

evidence.quote: we ablate the plan proposal and execution by asking a human volunteer to strictly follow the proposed plan and interact with the world
evidence.support_explanation: Real-world scenarios have no robot; a human executes the plan.

evidence.quote: in real world experiments, we currently use a perfect controller
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede the real-world part uses a perfect controller.

evidence.quote: it fails to provide the correct answer (e.g., Obs 5,7,9,11)
evidence.support_explanation: Failure case: H gives wrong/uninformative answers and the agent stalls.

evidence.quote: As shown in Figure 5 , the agent wrongly assume that the eggs in the garbagecan cannot be used to finish the task
evidence.support_explanation: Failure case analysis is qualitative (two cases).

evidence.quote: # Questions ALFWorld 1.1 ALFWorld with ambiguous tasks 1.39 Multiround ALFWorld 2.53
evidence.support_explanation: Average number of questions asked in successful episodes (human burden proxy).

evidence.quote: This requires a specical treatment to the data and we explicitly implement this for clarity
evidence.support_explanation: Multiround 'don't re-ask' behaviour is hand-implemented (explicit self-query) rather than emergent.

evidence.quote: we are the pioneers in addressing the challenge of enabling information gathering for embodied decision-making with LLM agents
evidence.support_explanation: Priority claim; neighbours cited but not compared.

evidence.quote: engages humans in active scene description
evidence.support_explanation: Closest neighbour (Huang et al. 2022b, Inner Monologue) described; no head-to-head run.

evidence.quote: For ReAct and ABA, we use K=2 in-context examples
evidence.support_explanation: Matched number of in-context examples between ABA and ReAct.

evidence.quote: It also got stuck in loops
evidence.support_explanation: Qualitative ReAct failure trajectory (hallucinated 'found' statements, loops).

evidence.quote: BUTLER ( Shridhar et al., 2021 ) is an imitation learning based method without LLM
evidence.support_explanation: BUTLER is the trained non-LLM baseline; its best-of-8 numbers are copied from its paper.

signatures.object: an ask action added to an LLM agent's action space (think/ask/act) in ALFWorld and Ravens robot-arm tasks
signatures.information: text observations (ALFWorld) or oracle captions with ground-truth coordinates (robot arm); instruction; K=2 (ALFWorld) or K=1 manually written in-context trajectories with metadata/ask steps; answers from H (LLM given simulator ground-truth object placement)
signatures.operation: LLM emits a rationale ('metadata') then a natural-language question; H answers; the answer is appended to the history and used to choose the next action
signatures.output: environment actions (go to / take / move_to coordinates) after one or more asks
signatures.conditions: an answerer exists, is cheap and mostly right (72.5% on a 40-question check); ambiguity or hidden object locations are present
signatures.selection_rule_or_data: none; the model decides when to ask via in-context examples (Multiround adds an explicit self-query 'have I seen X' step)
signatures.persistence: history within the episode; Multiround keeps knowledge across tasks inside one room
signatures.later_use: agent re-reads earlier answers/observations through the self-query when a later task needs the object
signatures.claimed_effect: higher success and shorter trajectories than ReAct with the same backbone
signatures.failure_boundary: H errors or uninformative answers stall the agent; agent can wrongly conclude an object is unusable

signatures.object: ABA-FT: Vicuna-7B LoRA finetuned on D_QA (ask-or-not QA about 'have you seen X') and D_pi (policy with corrupted actions masked)
signatures.information: expert (privileged) PDDL trajectories and simulator ground truth produce templated questions and CoT; student sees only its own observations and the answers
signatures.operation: teacher-forced SFT of one LLM for all tasks of an environment variant
signatures.output: a student that asks and acts without ICL examples
signatures.conditions: expert policy can be written from PDDL/ground truth; 1500 (Ambiguous) / 500 (Multiround) trajectories
signatures.selection_rule_or_data: noise injected with p=0.2 and masked out of the policy loss
signatures.later_use: used in the Ambiguous / Multiround evaluation
signatures.claimed_effect: ABA-FT > ABA, especially in long-horizon Multiround

gap.author_gap: Frontier-model agents deployed in unfamiliar environments or with vague instructions explore inefficiently and fail; humans ask peers instead.
gap.checked_gap: ReAct's qualitative failure (loops, hallucinated finds) and its collapse as the number of required answers grows (robot arm 95% -> 5%) support an information-gathering problem in this setting; but the baseline never receives the oracle information ABA is allowed to ask for.
lineage: ReAct / SayCan / Inner Monologue (LLM agents with think/act, scene feedback) -> ABA (open-domain natural-language querying as an action, metadata ICL, FT)
NAV/IL ask-for-oracle-action work (Nguyen & Daume, Singh et al.) = what ABA replaces with free-form language

closest_adjacent.name: Inner Monologue (Huang et al. 2022b)
closest_adjacent.solved: engages humans for scene, task or preference descriptions

closest_adjacent.name: Ren et al. 2023 (concurrent)
closest_adjacent.solved: explicit uncertainty module to trigger asking

gap.residue: How much of the gain comes from learning when/what to ask (the metadata mechanism) versus simply having an oracle channel is not separated; a prompt-given-all-information or exhaustive-exploration control is absent.
gap.stakes: Efficiency and success of embodied LLM agents when instructions are ambiguous or the environment is unknown.
gap.method_response: Treat asking as a first-class action, teach its rationale via metadata examples or finetuning, and answer with an external information source.
gap.remaining_gap: Reliability of the answerer (72.5%), real robot execution (human/perfect controller), over-asking cost, and uncertainty about when to stop asking (authors + ours).
gap.unresolved: Neighbour papers are not pinned; 'pioneers' priority claim cannot be checked from the materials.

rs_pattern.reason: Read the 15 main cards and checked decompose_and_delegate (no sound external solver: the 'solver' is a small LLM playing a human), assumption_audit_and_pivot (cards concern theoretical/security assumptions and sub-cards C01/C05/C11/C19/C28/C29 are proof, security and selection loci), reframe_as_solvable_object (no solver or guarantee imported from the formal Contextual-MDP restatement) and adapt_via_conditioning/C03 (no task-family conditioning substrate or category-level holdout). The operation - give an LLM agent a natural-language ask action backed by an external information source, teach it when to ask via rationale-augmented examples or SFT - is not defined by any original card, so outside_taxonomy is recorded without forcing a label.

claims.text: ABA improves success and efficiency over baseline LLM agents in ALFWorld.
claims.setting: ALFWorld ID/OOD, Vicuna-7B (5 seeds) and GPT-3.5 (3 seeds), K=2
claims.baseline_control: ReAct (same LLM/K/scoring), BUTLER (IL, best-of-8, 10^5 trajectories per task)
claims.selection_vs_test: ID and OOD splits of ALFWorld; in-context examples hand-written by the authors (source scenes not stated)
claims.result_denominator: ABA/G35 84 ID, 85 OOD vs ReAct/G35 64 ID, 65 OOD; ABA/V7B 56/48 vs ReAct 7/6; 6.3 vs 13.1 physical actions
claims.allowed_conclusion: With an LLM-played informant given ground-truth placement, asking raises ALFWorld success by ~20 (GPT-3.5) to ~40+ (Vicuna) points over ReAct and shortens trajectories; the gain bundles the oracle information.

claims.text: ABA and ABA-FT handle ambiguity and multi-round memory; FT helps long horizons.
claims.selection_vs_test: variants designed so that asking is necessary; ID/OOD legends in Fig 2
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported, favourable by construction, numbers unreadable from the text.

claims.text: ABA controls low-level pick-and-place by reasoning from language answers.
claims.setting: Ravens UR5e simulation, numeric coordinates, GPT-4, oracle caption module
claims.selection_vs_test: random placements per trial; per-task prompts
claims.result_denominator: 20 trials per setting; ABA 85-100% vs ReAct 5-95%, worst at y=4 (90 vs 5)
claims.allowed_conclusion: In oracle-perception simulation with a stated question budget, asking beats trial-and-error on three block-placement task families.

claims.text: ABA works in real-world open-domain image-based embodied tasks.
claims.setting: 3 qualitative scenarios, InstructBLIP captions + GPT-4, human executes
claims.allowed_conclusion: Qualitative demonstration of grounded question generation only; no embodied execution evidence.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: closed-loop simulator-judged success (ALFWorld, Ravens); robot-arm perception is privileged and real-world part has no robot; per-environment hand-made examples -> not transfer (EVIDENCE rules 2-3)
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In ALFWorld and a Ravens block-placement simulator, an LLM agent given an ask action and an LLM informant that holds the ground-truth object layout beats a no-ask ReAct with the same backbone and examples on success and trajectory length; the gain cannot be attributed to the metadata/learning mechanism and does not extend to real robots.
assessment.author_claim_kept: ABA and ABA-FT give substantial advantages in performance and efficiency across text-based household, robot arm and real-world open-domain tasks.
assessment.retention: not_applicable: ABA-FT is a static finetune of the student; no harness-revision retention claim
not_claimable: advantage over a baseline that is given the same information
unresolved: scope borderline: thin harness, text/oracle-caption environments, no robot hardware
ALFWorld ID/OOD sizes not stated in the text
whether OOD is free of example-development overlap

G.reason: Concrete, important gap (underspecified instructions and inefficient exploration) with a measurable ReAct failure profile; nearest neighbours (Inner Monologue, uncertainty-triggered asking) are named but not run, and the 'pioneers' claim is overreaching.

M.reason: Clear mechanism (ask action + rationale metadata + QA finetune) tightly tied to the gap and giving testable predictions (fewer actions, ask-before-explore); key assumption of a reliable answerer is weak (72.5%) and the metadata rationale is never contrasted with plain asking.

X.reason: Interaction format, ICL construction, H prompt, ABA-FT data recipe (noise 0.2, LoRA r=16, steps) and Multiround self-query are specified in appendices; full ABA prompts, scoring details of action selection and the Ravens prompts are shown only through examples, and the Multiround behaviour is hand-implemented.

measurement.reason: Simulator-judged success with seeds (5/3), mean +- std on ALFWorld and 20 trials per robot-arm configuration; but ID/OOD sizes not given, Ambiguous/Multiround numbers are figure-only, H accuracy is only 40 questions, and the real-world part has no counts.

causality.reason: ReAct vs ABA is a genuine same-backbone contrast, but ABA alone receives an oracle-informed channel (and variants are built so that asking is required), the metadata/QA mechanism is not ablated, and no all-information-in-prompt or exploration baseline separates information from agent design.

holdout.reason: ALFWorld OOD split exists and ABA keeps its gain there, but examples are hand-written per environment, robot-arm tasks use per-task prompts with oracle captions, no new embodiment/simulator is held out, contamination is undiscussed and the real-world part is not an embodied trial.

statistics.reason: Seeds with std for the main table, efficiency std, 20 trials for robot tasks and qualitative failure analysis; no CIs/paired tests and no quantified failure breakdown.

cost.reason: Trajectory length, action counts, questions per episode and finetune data fraction are reported, giving a human-burden proxy; tokens, calls to the informant, latency, USD and finetuning compute are absent and the informant is not priced.

status_reason: Full text incl. appendices read; outside_taxonomy recorded with reasons; figure-only numbers kept as unresolved.
